prompt: Indicate the correct statement regarding anatomic relationships of the esophagus:
options: It begins at the level of the thyroid cartilage
In the superior mediastinum, the left brachiocephalic vein constricts the esophagus
It passes through the diaphragm at the T8 level
In the posterior mediastinum, it passes anterior to the aorta before crossing the diaphragm
In the posterior mediastinum, it lies posterior to the right atrium
answer_text: In the posterior mediastinum, it passes anterior to the aorta before crossing the diaphragm
rationale: The oesophagus passes through the diaphragm at T10 and, low in the posterior mediastinum, sweeps anterior to the descending aorta. It lies posterior to the left atrium, not the right atrium.

prompt: The gallbladder lies in its fossa between which two anatomic lobes of the liver?
answer_text: Right and quadrate lobes
rationale: The gallbladder fossa lies on the visceral surface between the right lobe and the quadrate lobe.

prompt: Which of the following statements concerning liver sinusoids is true?
options: They are continuous with bile canaliculi
They are surrounded by a continuous basal lamina
They deliver blood to the central vein
They are lined by non-fenestrated endothelial cells
They perfuse only hepatocytes of the peripheral zone
answer_text: They deliver blood to the central vein
rationale: Hepatic sinusoids carry mixed portal and arterial blood toward the central vein. Their endothelium is fenestrated and they do not have a continuous basal lamina.

prompt: Which statement best describes the blood supply of the stomach?
options: It is derived entirely from the superior mesenteric artery
The gastroepiploic arteries supply the lesser curvature
The right gastric artery is a direct branch of the coeliac trunk
The short gastric arteries arise from the splenic artery
The left gastroepiploic artery arises directly from the coeliac trunk
answer_text: The short gastric arteries arise from the splenic artery
rationale: The short gastric arteries arise from the splenic artery and supply the fundus of the stomach.

prompt: Which statement about the borders of the epiploic foramen is correct?
options: The common bile duct is contained within the anterior border
The second part of the duodenum forms the inferior border
The quadrate lobe of the liver forms the superior border
The hepatic vein forms the posterior border
Not visible in the uploaded photograph
answer_text: The common bile duct is contained within the anterior border
rationale: The anterior boundary of the epiploic foramen is the hepatoduodenal ligament, which contains the portal triad including the common bile duct.

prompt: Which of the following statements best describes the colon?
options: The majority is derived from the primitive hindgut
It is usually invested with peritoneum on all sides
The ascending and descending colon are primarily retroperitoneal
The appendices epiploicae are composed of lymphoid tissue
Its three taenia are formed by the outer longitudinal layer of the muscularis externa
answer_text: Its three taenia are formed by the outer longitudinal layer of the muscularis externa
rationale: The three taeniae coli are condensations of the outer longitudinal layer of the muscularis externa. The ascending and descending colon are secondarily, not primarily, retroperitoneal.

prompt: Which statement about the dorsal spinocerebellar tract is accurate?
options: It lies lateral to the lateral corticospinal tract
It begins at about the level of the second or third lumbar segment
It passes through the inferior cerebellar peduncle
It terminates ipsilaterally in the cerebellar vermis
answer_text: All of the above
rationale: All four statements are standard features of the dorsal spinocerebellar tract: it lies lateral to the lateral corticospinal tract, begins around L2-L3, enters through the inferior cerebellar peduncle, and terminates ipsilaterally in the vermis/paravermis.

prompt: Which one of the following secretions is attributed to the Sertoli cells?
answer_text: Transferrin
rationale: Sertoli cells synthesize substances including transferrin, inhibin, androgen-binding protein and anti-Mullerian hormone. Testosterone is produced by Leydig cells.

prompt: Cancer of the testis most likely metastasizes first to which of the following lymph nodes?
answer_text: Lumbar
rationale: Testicular lymph follows the gonadal vessels to the lumbar (para-aortic) lymph nodes.

prompt: The adrenal gland:
options: Secretes cortisol from the zona glomerulosa of the cortex
Is supplied by branches of the inferior phrenic artery, the renal artery, and the aorta
Is drained by the suprarenal vein reaching the inferior vena cava on the left and the renal vein on the right
answer_text: Is supplied by branches of the inferior phrenic artery, the renal artery, and the aorta
rationale: The suprarenal gland receives superior, middle and inferior suprarenal arteries from the inferior phrenic artery, aorta and renal artery. Cortisol is mainly from zona fasciculata, and venous drainage is right to IVC and left to left renal vein.

prompt: Which of the following is the major source of serotonin in the CNS?
answer_text: Raphe nuclei
rationale: The raphe nuclei are the major serotonergic nuclei of the CNS.

prompt: The structure that separates the quadrate lobe from the left lobe of the liver is the:
answer_text: Round ligament (ligamentum teres)
rationale: On the visceral surface, the quadrate lobe is separated from the left lobe by the fissure containing the round ligament (ligamentum teres).

prompt: The right lung:
options: Has an impression of the azygos arch on its medial surface
Has a horizontal fissure separating the lower from the middle lobe
Is in contact with the pericardium overlying the right ventricle
answer_text: Has an impression of the azygos arch on its medial surface
rationale: The right lung has a groove/impression for the arch of the azygos vein. Its horizontal fissure separates upper from middle lobe, and its major cardiac impression is related to the right atrium.

prompt: The nerve supplying the facial muscles innervates also the following muscle:
answer_text: Stylohyoid
rationale: The facial nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression and also the stylohyoid, posterior belly of digastric and stapedius.

prompt: Which of the following nerves is responsible for carrying the sensation of pain from the laryngeal vestibule?
answer_text: Superior laryngeal nerve
rationale: Sensation from the laryngeal mucosa above the vocal folds, including the vestibule, is carried mainly by the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.

prompt: The neurons providing the sensation of taste in the anterior 2/3 of the tongue are found in which of the following?
answer_text: Geniculate ganglion
rationale: Taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue travels in the chorda tympani; the primary sensory neuron cell bodies are in the geniculate ganglion.

prompt: Which of the following drains into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity?
answer_text: Nasolacrimal duct
rationale: The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior nasal meatus.

prompt: In the thorax, the right vagus:
options: Lies anterior to the root of the lung
Gives rise to the right recurrent laryngeal nerve
Contributes to the formation of the oesophageal plexus
answer_text: Contributes to the formation of the oesophageal plexus
rationale: In the thorax the right vagus passes posterior to the lung root and contributes to the oesophageal plexus. The right recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks around the right subclavian artery near the thoracic inlet/root of the neck.

prompt: Which of the following statements concerning antral ovarian follicles is true?
options: They have a single layer of cuboidal follicular cells surrounding the oocyte
answer_text: Their continued maturation requires FSH
rationale: Antral follicle growth and continued maturation depend on FSH. Antral follicles contain liquor folliculi, multiple granulosa layers and theca interna/externa.

prompt: Nerve terminals that synapse in the adrenal medulla utilize which neurotransmitter?
answer_text: Acetylcholine
rationale: Preganglionic sympathetic fibres synapsing on adrenal medullary chromaffin cells release acetylcholine.

prompt: Which of the following statements concerning the basal nuclei is true?
options: The caudate nucleus is not connected to the lentiform nucleus
The corpus striatum receives fibers from the compact part of the substantia nigra
The lentiform nucleus is separated from the thalamus by the external capsule
The lentiform nucleus is separated from the claustrum by the internal capsule
The tail of the caudate nucleus lies in the occipital lobe
answer_text: The corpus striatum receives fibers from the compact part of the substantia nigra
rationale: The striatum receives the nigrostriatal dopaminergic projection from substantia nigra pars compacta.

prompt: The fovea of the retina contains:
options: Rods as photoreceptors and blood vessels
Cones as photoreceptors and no blood vessels
Cones as photoreceptors and blood vessels
Rods and cones but no blood vessels
Rods and cones and blood vessels
answer_text: Cones as photoreceptors and no blood vessels
rationale: The fovea is specialized for high-acuity vision: it contains cones and is avascular.

prompt: Which of the following statements regarding the cerebral cortex is true?
options: The primary motor cortex lies in the frontal lobe
The primary somatosensory cortex lies in the frontal lobe
The primary auditory cortex lies in the parietal lobe
The primary visual cortex lies in the frontal lobe
Broca's speech area lies in the parietal lobe
answer_text: The primary motor cortex lies in the frontal lobe
rationale: The primary motor cortex is the precentral gyrus of the frontal lobe.

prompt: Which of the following statements accurately describes relations at the left lung hilum?
options: The left pulmonary artery is the most anterior structure
The left bronchus passes under the aortic arch
The left vagus nerve passes anterior to the hilum
Pulmonary veins are posterior and inferior
The left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops around the left pulmonary artery
answer_text: The left bronchus passes under the aortic arch
rationale: At the left hilum the pulmonary artery lies superior to the bronchus, and the left main bronchus passes beneath the aortic arch. The vagus is posterior to the root and pulmonary veins are mainly anterior/inferior.

prompt: Which of the following statements best describes the uterine cervix?
options: In a normally anteflexed uterus, the cervix is tilted posteriorly
It makes up the inferior third of the uterus
Vaginal fornices surround its supravaginal part
It is the attachment site for the round ligament
It communicates with the uterine cavity through the external os
answer_text: It makes up the inferior third of the uterus
rationale: The cervix forms the lower third of the uterus. The vaginal fornices surround its vaginal part, and the uterine cavity communicates with the cervical canal through the internal os.

prompt: Regarding the ventricular system and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) production, which of the following statements is true?
options: CSF is exclusively produced in the choroid plexi of the lateral ventricles
CSF passes from the 3rd to the 4th ventricle via the interventricular foramen
The 4th ventricle communicates directly with the subarachnoid space
The total daily production of CSF is approximately 150 ml
CSF is reabsorbed mainly through the arachnoid villi in the inferior sagittal sinus
answer_text: The 4th ventricle communicates directly with the subarachnoid space
rationale: The fourth ventricle communicates directly with the subarachnoid space through the median and lateral apertures. CSF production is roughly 500 mL/day and reabsorption is mainly via arachnoid granulations into dural venous sinuses, especially the superior sagittal sinus.

prompt: Which statement about the tracts of the spinal cord is accurate?
options: The majority of motor fibers descend in the anterior column of the cord
The spinothalamic tract subserves pain sensation
The gracile tract lies lateral to the cuneate tract
The spinothalamic tract carries first-order sensory neurones
The dorsal columns carry decussated fibers
answer_text: The spinothalamic tract subserves pain sensation
rationale: The spinothalamic system carries pain and temperature. Its ascending fibres are second-order neurons after crossing in the spinal cord.

prompt: Which of the following statements accurately describes the relations of the ureter?
options: It is crossed anteriorly by the gonadal vessels
It crosses the brim of the pelvis at the bifurcation of the common iliac artery
In females it passes under the uterine artery close to the cervix
It enters the bladder at the posterolateral aspect of the trigone
All of the above are correct
answer_text: All of the above are correct
rationale: All listed relations are standard: gonadal vessels cross anteriorly, the ureter crosses the pelvic brim near the common iliac bifurcation, passes under the uterine artery near the cervix, and enters the bladder at a posterolateral angle of the trigone.

prompt: Which of the following statements concerning the structure of medullary rays in the kidney is true?
options: They do not extend into the renal cortex
They lie at the center of a renal lobule
They contain thin limbs of the loops of Henle
answer_text: They lie at the center of a renal lobule
rationale: A renal lobule is centered on a medullary ray. Medullary rays contain straight tubules and collecting ducts extending into the cortex, not renal corpuscles or convoluted tubules.

prompt: Which statement about the substantia nigra is accurate?
options: The ventral part consists of pigmented neurons that contain neuromelanin granules
The dorsal part contains mostly GABAergic neurons
It is subdivided into a dorsal pars compacta and a ventral pars reticulata
The ventral part contains mostly dopaminergic neurons
answer_text: It is subdivided into a dorsal pars compacta and a ventral pars reticulata
rationale: The substantia nigra is divided into a dorsal pars compacta and ventral pars reticulata. Pars compacta contains pigmented dopaminergic neurons; pars reticulata is predominantly GABAergic.
